stories.title: Black Hat Asia 2026 | Discovering React2Shell: JavaScript’s Long-Awaited Deserialization Flight-mare
stories.abstract: A critical deserialization vulnerability, dubbed React2Shell (CVE-2025-55182), affects a widely used JavaScript framework. The flaw enables remote code execution by exploiting complex object handling within the V8 engine and Node.js runtime, leading to massive exploitation attempts across the internet.
stories.why: It demonstrates that modern JavaScript frameworks are susceptible to classic deserialization attacks, posing a severe risk to high-traffic web infrastructure.
stories.action: Identify and patch affected React-based applications immediately.

stories.title: Microsoft Patches 398 Flaws Including a Windows Driver Zero-Day Under Active Attack
stories.abstract: Microsoft addressed a critical zero-day vulnerability, CVE-2026-68820, within the Windows kernel. The flaw, dubbed LegacyHive, allows attackers who have already gained initial access to a system to escalate their privileges to SYSTEM level by exploiting network socket operations.
stories.why: This vulnerability is actively exploited in the wild, posing a significant risk for lateral movement and full system compromise following initial infection.
stories.action: Apply the July 2026 security updates to all Windows systems immediately.

stories.title: Cisco ASA and FTD Flaw Exploited in the Wild Can Trigger Remote DoS
stories.abstract: Cisco has confirmed active exploitation of a high-severity vulnerability, CVE-2026-20349, affecting the Remote Access SSL VPN functionality in ASA and FTD software. Unauthenticated attackers can trigger a denial-of-service condition by sending specifically crafted HTTP requests to the targeted devices.
stories.why: This flaw is actively exploited in the wild and has been added to CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, indicating high risk to perimeter infrastructure.
stories.action: Apply the latest security patches provided by Cisco immediately.

stories.title: Hitachi Energy APM Edge Product
stories.abstract: Hitachi Energy has disclosed two critical vulnerabilities, CVE-2026-43284 and CVE-2026-43500, affecting APM Edge versions 6.10 and earlier. These flaws, involving write-what-where conditions and out-of-bounds writes, could allow attackers to compromise the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the industrial software.
stories.why: These vulnerabilities impact critical infrastructure and carry high CVSS scores, posing significant risks to operational technology environments.
stories.action: Review Hitachi Energy's advisory and apply the recommended patches or mitigations for APM Edge.

stories.title: 1.6M RingCentral accounts' data dumped after ShinyHunters extortion attack
stories.abstract: The ShinyHunters extortion group leaked personal data belonging to 1.6 million RingCentral users. The exposed information includes names, physical addresses, email addresses, and phone numbers, following a security compromise that occurred in July.
stories.why: Large-scale exposure of contact information significantly increases the risk of targeted phishing, social engineering, and identity theft for affected users.

stories.title: SAP Commerce Cloud Flaw Could Let Unauthenticated Attackers Execute Arbitrary Code
stories.abstract: A critical remote code execution vulnerability in SAP Commerce Cloud, tracked as CVE-2026-58231, is currently being exploited in the wild. The flaw stems from inadequate authorization and input validation, allowing attackers to execute arbitrary code on affected systems.
stories.why: The vulnerability carries a maximum CVSS score of 10.0 and active exploitation indicates an immediate risk to unpatched enterprise commerce environments.
stories.action: Apply the latest SAP security patches immediately.

stories.title: Stopping a cyberattack while walking your dog - defensive AI security CEO says it's not ruff to do
stories.abstract: The CEO of startup Corma claims their new defensive AI platform provides security teams with a unified, automated interface to manage and mitigate cyber threats, effectively allowing administrators to oversee complex security operations from mobile devices.
stories.why: Centralized AI-driven orchestration tools aim to reduce response times, though they introduce new dependencies on third-party security automation logic.

stories.title: Hackers Exploiting Unpatched GeoServer Zero-Day
stories.abstract: Threat actors are actively exploiting a critical SQL injection vulnerability within GeoServer. This flaw enables unauthenticated remote code execution, potentially granting attackers full control over affected servers.
stories.why: Remote code execution vulnerabilities in geospatial data infrastructure pose significant risks to data integrity and internal network access.
stories.action: Identify and isolate GeoServer instances; apply vendor-supplied patches immediately.

stories.title: New Evooo1Bot Linux botnet turns routers into traffic relay nodes
stories.abstract: A Mirai-derived botnet dubbed Evooo1Bot is actively compromising internet-facing gateway devices. The malware transforms these routers into persistent SOCKS5 proxies, allowing attackers to route malicious traffic through compromised infrastructure to evade detection.
stories.why: Compromised edge devices serve as stealthy entry points for lateral movement and obfuscated attacks against internal network resources.
stories.action: Ensure all gateway devices are updated and disable unnecessary remote management services.

stories.title: AWS key exposed in JavaScript may have lit way to Beacon's charity data
stories.abstract: CRM provider Beacon suffered a data breach affecting over 1,000 charities after an AWS access key was inadvertently exposed within public JavaScript build artifacts. Unauthorized parties accessed and likely downloaded the customer database containing sensitive information.
stories.why: Exposed credentials in client-side code remain a critical supply chain risk, leading to unauthorized cloud infrastructure access and large-scale data exfiltration.

stories.title: How to tell if your AI platforms’ accounts have been hacked
stories.abstract: A new guide outlines methods for users to identify potential unauthorized access or account compromises across major artificial intelligence platforms, helping individuals detect if their credentials have been exposed or misused by malicious actors.
stories.why: AI accounts often contain sensitive proprietary data or API keys, making them high-value targets for credential stuffing and unauthorized resource exploitation.

stories.title: HashiCorp security advisory (AV26-817)
stories.abstract: Recent security advisories highlight critical vulnerabilities across several platforms. HashiCorp's Vault Secrets Operator (pre-1.5.0) faces arbitrary file read risks, Zimbra Collaboration (pre-10.1.20) requires patching, and Plesk (CVE-2026-64639) is susceptible to privilege escalation through database cloning.
stories.why: These flaws allow unauthorized file access or administrative control, posing significant risks to infrastructure and server management environments.
stories.action: Update Vault Secrets Operator to 1.5.0, Zimbra to 10.1.20, and Plesk to 18.0.80.2 or 18.0.79.6.

stories.title: Autonomous AI attacks pose 'clear and present danger' to critical infrastructure
stories.abstract: Security researchers warn that autonomous AI agents could soon facilitate sophisticated cyberattacks against critical infrastructure. These automated systems may accelerate the speed and scale of digital intrusions, potentially resulting in physical damage to industrial control systems and essential public services.
stories.why: Automated, AI-driven exploitation could bypass traditional defensive response times, increasing the risk of catastrophic failure in operational technology environments.

stories.title: Attackers Exploit VMware vCenter Vulnerability to Gain Persistent Remote Access
stories.abstract: Attackers are actively exploiting CVE-2026-59310, a critical directory-traversal vulnerability in VMware vCenter Server. The flaw allows remote, unauthenticated code execution. Security researchers warn that applying the vendor-provided patch may be insufficient to fully remediate the threat in compromised environments.
stories.why: Remote code execution in core infrastructure management software poses a severe risk of lateral movement and full environment compromise.
stories.action: Apply the latest VMware vCenter security patches and conduct thorough post-patching compromise assessments.
